summary: Skill usage is easier to check and explain. Wombat recognizes verified native Skill reads, shows concise activity summaries, and can trace or recompute a selected count without a background service.
highlights: See whether a Skill was used in the selected period, with short default reports and detailed counting evidence available on demand.

Inspect included and excluded records with check skills --explain, select one item, or locate unassigned operations. Explanations include original conversation positions and actual counting contributions.

Save an explanation and pass it back with --baseline to recompute the same selection. Comparisons distinguish result changes from changed evidence, configuration or scope; paginated differences disclose their coverage.

Count verified native terminal reads of SKILL.md while keeping catalog listings, declined executions, user-shell commands and unverified shell classifications separate. Failed dispatched reads still count.
Preserve committed usage counts on cached queries and unrelated configuration metadata during category-specific discovery.
Read requested configuration categories first, so a large project instruction walk cannot exhaust discovery before known Skills are found.
Filter stored ledger groups and unrelated operation frames before decoding, reuse turn associations and borrow existing facts. Token and pricing accounting are unchanged.
knownLimitations: Detailed explanations use bounded pages; unresolved targets remain available for investigation rather than being assigned to arbitrary Skills.
Recomputation uses current rules over normalized local facts. It does not execute recorded commands, call models, or run historical parser versions.
The configuration protocol is now v3 and use-counting method v4. Update the CLI, plugin and integrations together; previous protocol results are rejected without compatibility aliases.
Local CLI analysis does not upload conversations. Selected Skill evidence enters the current Codex conversation. Codex artifact cleanup remains limited to supported macOS layouts.
